text:
Accuracy check, Response A: "tested above the legal Legionella threshold on 29 September" is fine (sample taken 29 Sept). "When results arrived on 3 October, we notified the health department within the required 24 hours, then shut down and disinfected" is accurate. "Resample was clear" is correct. "Contractor missed a monthly visit without telling us" is accurate. The pump failure is said to follow the missed visit, whereas the report says the pump failed mid-September and wasn't picked up because the visit was missed. "The biocide dosing pump failed after the contractor missed a monthly visit" reverses the sequence slightly, a minor causal ambiguity. Other points are correct. Word count is approximately 125? Let me count roughly: Decision (24) + What happened (~58) + Cause (~19) + Next steps (~32) ≈ 133. It may exceed 120 words.

Response B: "The contractor had visited monthly and missed this fault during those visits" is inaccurate: the monthly visit was missed, not the fault missed during visits. That is a substantive error, as it misattributes the cause. It also says "we notified the health department within 24 hours" without noting it was of results, fine. Also "returned to service after the resample" is OK. Word count is clearly over 120 (~220 words). It also has filler ("I am writing to provide an update", "We appreciate your attention").

Both probably exceed the limit, but B far more so. B has a factual error about the cause. A is better on accuracy, concision, and leads with the decision.

Verdict: A
